page.layout: One column of verse, centred and indented, running from the top to the ornament; below it a printed ornament and the catchword "EIVS-" at the right. No margin notes. Running head at the top right of the page above the text.

l.i: En erit, ut tecum, iudicio Dei
Urbs sancta, cui sic posse fauces

page.notes: The first line of the verse is printed as "Perpetuas IOVAE dicere gratias:", with the word "gratias" followed by a colon. Several lines show printing irregularities which I have left as printed: "Perenne nomen,luculentis", "fuenit", "Iniuriosis & socium & suis" and "Ensiferam,& neruos" are as printed. The word "Quales" at the start of line 2 has a decorative capital Q. The ornament between the verse and the catchword is a printed woodcut fleuron and is not transcribed as text. The verse rendering is an approximation of the printed line breaks; the Greek-free text contains no Hebrew or Greek. Some words in the middle of the poem ("Confisus", "infanire", "fuetis") are doubtful and should be checked against the scan.
